protocol: BACnet/IP (Annex J) — Confirmed-Request ReadProperty and its ComplexACK, over UDP/47808, with the BVLC + NPDU + APDU stack, context/application tag encoding, extended lengths, opening/closing constructed tags, and APDU segmentation.

captures.label: C1 — Client → Device: BACnet-Confirmed-Request-PDU, ReadProperty (analog-input,1).object-name
captures.fieldBreakdown:
0:1:bvlc.type:0x81 (BACnet/IP)
1:1:bvlc.function:0x0a (Original-Unicast-NPDU)
2:2:bvlc.length:0x0011 = 17 — length of the ENTIRE BVLL message INCLUDING these 4 header octets
4:1:npdu.version:0x01
5:1:npdu.control:0x04 (bit7=0 → NSDU is an APDU; bit6=0 reserved; bit5=0 → no DNET/DLEN/DADR; bit4=0 reserved; bit3=0 → no SNET/SLEN/SADR; bit2=1 → expecting-reply; bits1-0=00 → priority Normal)
6:1:apdu.pduTypeFlags:0x02 (bits7-4=0000 → Confirmed-Request; bit3 SEG=0; bit2 MOR=0; bit1 SA=1 segmented-response-accepted; bit0=0 reserved)
7:1:apdu.maxSegsMaxApdu:0x25 (bit7=0 reserved; bits6-4=010 → max-segments-accepted code 2 = 4 segments; bits3-0=0101 → max-APDU-length-accepted code 5 = 1476 octets)
8:1:apdu.invokeId:0x01
9:1:apdu.serviceChoice:0x0c = 12 (readProperty)
10:1:tag.ctx0:0x0c (bits7-4=0000 tag number 0 = objectIdentifier; bit3=1 class=context-specific; bits2-0=100 LVT=4 → 4 value octets)
11:4:objectIdentifier:0x00000001 (bits31-22 = 0 → object-type analog-input; bits21-0 = 1 → instance 1)
15:1:tag.ctx1:0x19 (tag number 1 = propertyIdentifier; class=context-specific; LVT=1 → 1 value octet)
16:1:propertyIdentifier:0x4d = 77 (object-name)
captures.notes: 17 octets total. Legal chosen values (not from a real trace, but canonically correct): invoke ID 0x01, max-APDU-length-accepted code 5 (=1476 octets), max-segments-accepted code 2 (=4 segments), segmented-response-accepted = 1. UDP src/dst port 47808 (0xBAC0), unicast. BVLC length 0x0011 = 17 and the emitted datagram is 17 octets — checked.

captures.label: C2 — Device → Client: BACnet-ComplexACK-PDU, unsegmented, ReadProperty-ACK carrying a CharacterString

0:1:bvlc.type:0x81 (BACnet/IP)
1:1:bvlc.function:0x0a (Original-Unicast-NPDU)
2:2:bvlc.length:0x0020 = 32 (whole BVLL incl. these 4 octets)
4:1:npdu.version:0x01
5:1:npdu.control:0x00 (APDU; no DNET; no SNET; expecting-reply=0; priority Normal)
6:1:apdu.pduTypeFlags:0x30 (bits7-4=0011 → ComplexACK; bit3 SEG=0; bit2 MOR=0; bits1-0=00 reserved)
7:1:apdu.invokeId:0x01 (echoes C1)
8:1:apdu.serviceAckChoice:0x0c = 12 (readProperty)
9:1:tag.ctx0:0x0c (tag number 0, context class, LVT=4)
10:4:objectIdentifier:0x00000001 (analog-input, instance 1)
14:1:tag.ctx1:0x19 (tag number 1, context class, LVT=1)
15:1:propertyIdentifier:0x4d = 77 (object-name)
16:1:tag.ctx3.open:0x3e (tag number 3 = propertyValue; class=context; LVT=6 → OPENING tag, no length declared)
17:1:tag.app7:0x75 (bits7-4=0111 tag number 7 = Character String; bit3=0 class=application; bits2-0=101 LVT=5 → EXTENDED length follows)
18:1:extendedLength:0x0c = 12 value octets (escape rules: this octet, unless it is 254 → u16be follows, or 255 → u32be follows)
19:1:charstr.encoding:0x00 (character set ANSI X3.4 / UTF-8)
20:11:charstr.value:5a 6f 6e 65 20 33 20 54 65 6d 70 = "Zone 3 Temp"

This is the interesting one — the property value sits between an opening tag (0x3e) and a closing tag (0x3f) that carry NO length, and the CharacterString itself needs the extended-length escape (LVT=5, then one length octet = 12 = 1 charset octet + 11 text octets). BVLC length 0x0020 = 32 and the datagram is 32 octets — checked.

statefulness:
BACnet/IP breaks v0's state model in a specific way: it is CONNECTIONLESS, so `disconnected → connected → authenticated` is the wrong axis entirely. The unit of state is not a connection but a TRANSACTION keyed by invoke ID, and up to 255 of them can be live against one peer at once. v0's four scopes (state = one run, session = one connection, store = per device, seq = counter) have no slot for "per in-flight transaction", so segment windows, retry counts and timers for concurrent reads have nowhere to live.

WHAT IS LEGAL IN WHICH STATE. Per invoke ID: `idle → awaitingAck` on sending the Confirmed-Request. From `awaitingAck` the only legal inbound PDUs are SimpleACK, ComplexACK (SEG=0 → `complete`; SEG=1 → `receivingSegments`), Error, Reject, Abort, or a SegmentACK if the REQUEST was itself segmented. From `receivingSegments` the only legal inbound PDU is the next ComplexACK segment with sequenceNumber == last+1 mod 256, or an Abort. A segment out of window must be answered with a NAK SegmentACK (NAK bit set), not silently dropped. A second Confirmed-Request reusing a live invoke ID is illegal and the device is entitled to Abort. Globally: after DeviceCommunicationControl(disable), the device accepts ONLY DeviceCommunicationControl and ReinitializeDevice — a modal exclusive state.

WHAT MUST CHAIN. Segment N is meaningless without 0..N-1: the service payload is one octet stream cut at arbitrary boundaries (capture C3 stops mid-object-identifier), so nothing can be interpreted until MOR=0 arrives. Each segment must be SegmentACK'd before the sender will advance past the window. A write to a commandable object chains too — WriteProperty at a priority is only meaningful relative to the current priority array.

WHAT MUST NEVER COMBINE. SA=0 in the request forbids a segmented reply; a device that must segment anyway has to Abort with reason 4 (segmentation-not-supported) instead. Segments larger than the requested max-APDU-length-accepted, or more than max-segments-accepted of them, are likewise forbidden — the device must Abort (reason 1, buffer-overflow) rather than overrun. actual-window-size in the SegmentACK must be ≤ the proposed-window-size in the ComplexACK.

NEGOTIATED CAPABILITY (v0's listed gap, CONFIRMED and load-bearing here). The request PROPOSES three things — SA, max-APDU-length-accepted (code 5 = 1476 in C1), max-segments-accepted (code 2 = 4). The responder GRANTS less, or refuses. Then the responder counter-proposes a window size and the requester grants that down again in C4. Two rounds of grant-down in one exchange, and nothing in v0 records the outcome for the NEXT message to consult.

CONFIRMED vs PRESUMED. A ComplexACK confirms the property value AT THE INSTANT OF THE READ — for present-value on an analog input that is stale in seconds, so it is a confirmed fact with a very short TTL, not a durable one. The sharp case is the other direction: WriteProperty(present-value, priority 16) returns a SimpleACK meaning "the write was ACCEPTED", not "the output moved". If an existing priority-8 command holds the point, the output does not change and the ACK still says success. So a successful ACK confirms message acceptance and only PRESUMES effect; confirming the effect needs a readback of present-value, and DIAGNOSING a mismatch needs a second, different read (priority-array / relinquish-default). v0's `confirmedBy` allows only one message and one `matches` predicate. Device-instance → IP binding learned from I-Am is likewise presumed, with a TTL, because DHCP moves it.

DISCOVERED ONLY FROM THE NEXT RESPONSE. (1) Property unsupported — C5 Error(property, unknown-property) is the first and only signal; nothing in C1 could have predicted it. (2) Object deleted or the device reconfigured — Error(object, unknown-object) on a read that worked yesterday. (3) Device restarted mid-transaction — your outstanding invoke ID is answered by an Abort, or by nothing. (4) Segmentation unsupported — learned only from Abort AFTER the request. (5) The worst one: a device in DCC-disabled state, or behind a downed MS/TP router, returns SILENCE, which is byte-identical to a lost UDP datagram and to a dead device. Distinguishing them requires an out-of-band probe (Who-Is) and a policy, neither of which v0 can express — `onTimeout` maps a timeout to exactly one successor state, but here one timeout has three different meanings.

RETRANSMIT AND DEDUP. APDU_Retries reuses the SAME invoke ID, so the device must dedup and the client must tolerate duplicate ACKs for one logical read. Idempotent reads make this survivable; a retried WriteProperty on a non-idempotent object does not. v0 has `idempotent: true` as a flag but no dedup window and no retry policy attached to it.

SEQUENCE NUMBERS AND WINDOWS. The segment sequenceNumber is modulo 256 with a sliding window whose size is negotiated per transaction. v0 has `seq.next` (a monotonic persisted counter) and nothing else — no modulo, no window, no out-of-order/NAK handling.

gaps.what: `bits` cannot span more than one octet, has no decode form, and has no defined bit order.
gaps.why: The 32-bit BACnetObjectIdentifier is a 10-bit object-type followed by a 22-bit instance — `00 00 00 01` at C1 offset 11, `02 00 01 04` at C3 offset 12. Neither half is octet-aligned. §6 has no shl/shr/or, so the only route is a 32-bit `bits` group, and §3's sole example is 1+3+4 = exactly 8 bits with no statement that wider is legal. Worse, the decode example in §3 never shows `bits` with `as:` at all — so on decode every BACnet tag byte (4-bit number, 1-bit class, 3-bit LVT), the NPDU control octet, and APDU byte 0/1 are unsplittable.
gaps.proposedFix:
Extend `bits` to a documented multi-octet, MSB-first bit stream with a decode form:
{ "bits": [ {"n":10,"as":"objectType"}, {"n":22,"as":"instance"} ],
  "order":"msbFirst" }
Spec rules to add: components pack most-significant-first into a big-endian bit stream; the sum of n MUST be a multiple of 8; in decode mode each component takes `as:` and yields an Int; in encode mode each takes `value:`. A component may also carry `onReencode:"preserveCaptured"` (see the round-trip gap).

gaps.why: Three separate discriminators in one datagram. (a) BVLC function at offset 1 selects the body: 0x0a/0x0b → NPDU immediately; 0x04 Forwarded-NPDU inserts 6 octets first; 0x05 Register-Foreign-Device is a 2-octet TTL and no NPDU. (b) APDU byte 0's top nibble selects one of eight PDU layouts (0x02 in C1 = Confirmed-Request, 0x30 in C2 = ComplexACK, 0x40 in C4 = SegmentACK, 0x50 in C5 = Error). (c) Bit 3 of that same octet (0x3c in C3) inserts two extra header octets. v0's `when` gates ONE field's presence; it cannot select among alternative field LISTS, and §3 documents `when` only in encode mode.
gaps.proposedFix:
{ "switch": "capture.apduType",
  "cases": {
    "0": { "fields": [ /* Confirmed-Request */ ] },
    "3": { "fields": [ /* ComplexACK */ ] },
    "4": { "fields": [ /* SegmentACK */ ] },
    "5": { "fields": [ /* Error */ ] } },
  "default": { "fail": "unsupported APDU type" } }
Valid in both encode and decode; in encode the case is chosen by the same expression over `inputs.*`. Also state explicitly that `when` is legal on any decode field and is evaluated against `capture.*` decoded so far.

gaps.what: No predicate-terminated repetition, and no decoder-carried state — constructed data has no length at all.
gaps.why: C2 offsets 16..31: opening tag 0x3e (context 3, LVT=6) ... closing tag 0x3f (LVT=7). NOTHING between them declares how many octets they enclose, and they nest arbitrarily (a BACnetPropertyValue list is opening tags inside opening tags). The only correct parse is: push depth on LVT==6, pop on LVT==7, loop until depth returns to 0. v0's `each` takes a COUNT (`capture.byteCount / 2`), never a predicate; there is no loop-carried accumulator; and §3 explicitly frames decode as a per-field fold. §5 already flags decoder-carried state for CoAP option deltas — BACnet needs it in three independent places in the same datagram (tag depth, NPDU optional-field gating, the SEG bit changing header length).

gaps.what: No fragmentation/reassembly layer — segment boundaries are octet-arbitrary, so no segment is independently parseable.
gaps.why: C3 is 37 octets ending `... c4 00 00`. The 0xc4 at offset 34 declares 4 value octets; only 2 fit. The remaining 2 octets, any further list entries, and the closing tag 0x3f are in segment 1. The logical APDU that `parse` must run against is the concatenation of segment payloads, which is a byte stream that never appears on any wire. §5 lists this as a known gap; this capture shows it is worse than 'reassembly is missing' — it means the parse target is a synthetic buffer, and it also means ENCODE must materialise the whole payload before it knows how many datagrams it will emit or what each one's MOR bit and BVLC length will be.
gaps.proposedFix:
A reassembly/fragmentation layer sitting between the transport and the `bytes` layer:
{ "kind":"reassemble",
  "key":"capture.invokeId",
  "seq":"capture.sequenceNumber", "seqModulo":256,
  "more":"capture.moreFollows",
  "window":"capture.proposedWindowSize",
  "ackWith":"messages.segmentAck", "nakWith":"messages.segmentNak",
  "maxSegments":"inputs.maxSegCode", "timeoutMs":5000,
  "emit":"assembledApdu" }
The `parse` block then runs against `assembledApdu`, not the datagram. The encode direction is the same layer inverted: "fragment": { "mtu":"negotiated.maxApdu", "headerPerSegment": [ … ] }.

gaps.what: No minimal-length integer encoding, where the octet count is written into a bit-field of a byte already emitted.
gaps.why: BACnet unsigned/enumerated/signed use the FEWEST octets that hold the value, and that count IS the LVT nibble of the preceding tag octet. propertyId 77 → `19 4d` (LVT=1); propertyId 512 → `1a 02 00` (LVT=2); a proprietary 24-bit value → LVT=3. So encoding requires knowing the width of bytes not yet emitted and back-patching it into a BIT-FIELD, and decoding requires the width to come from a bit-field just read. v0's two-pass back-patching is defined only for whole scalars sized by span expressions, and `octets()` is not a span function.
gaps.proposedFix:
Add converters `minUint` / `minInt` (Int → Bytes, fewest octets) and a span function `octets(field:X)` usable inside a `bits` component, resolved in pass 2:
{ "bits":[ {"n":4,"value":"1"}, {"n":1,"value":"1"},
           {"n":3,"value":"octets(field:propVal)"} ] },
{ "value":"inputs.propertyId | minUint", "id":"propVal" }
Engine consequence to state explicitly: pass-2 back-patching must be able to target a bit-field component, not only a whole scalar.

gaps.what: No transaction scope in the state model.
gaps.why: BACnet/IP is connectionless UDP with up to 255 concurrent confirmed transactions per peer, each keyed by invoke ID (0x01 in C1/C2/C5, 0x02 in C3/C4), each with its own timer, retry counter, segment window, and legal-next-message set. v0 offers `state.*` (one run — too coarse, all transactions collide), `session.*` (one connection — there is no connection), `store.*` (per device — outlives the transaction) and `seq.*` (a bare counter). Nothing keys state by a value carried in the packet.
gaps.proposedFix:
"model": { "transaction": {
    "key":"capture.invokeId", "scope":"txn.*", "maxConcurrent":255,
    "timeoutMs":3000, "retries":3, "retryReusesKey":true, "dedupWindowMs":10000,
    "states": { "idle":{"initial":true},
                "awaitingAck":{"timeoutMs":3000,"onTimeout":"retryOrFail"},
                "receivingSegments":{"timeoutMs":5000},
                "complete":{"terminal":true} },
    "transitions": [
      {"from":"awaitingAck","to":"receivingSegments","when":"capture.seg == 1"},
      {"from":"receivingSegments","to":"receivingSegments",
       "when":"capture.sequenceNumber == (txn.lastSeq + 1) % 256"},
      {"from":"receivingSegments","to":"complete","when":"capture.mor == 0"} ] } }
This simultaneously supplies the missing dedup window and the sequence-number/window primitive §5 lists as gaps.

gaps.what: A length field that is inside the span it measures is not defined as legal or illegal.
gaps.why: BVLC length at offset 2 (0x0011 in C1, 0x0020 in C2) counts the ENTIRE BVLL message including the 4-octet BVLC header and therefore including itself. §3 says 'a cyclic span dependency is a validation error' but never says whether a field sitting inside its own span counts as cyclic. Mechanically it is resolvable — all widths are static, so pass 1 emits a 2-octet placeholder and pass 2 fills it — but a validator written to the letter of §3 would reject `len(group:bvll)` from inside `bvll`. This is not academic: Modbus/TCP's length EXCLUDES itself and BVLC's INCLUDES itself, so the grammar must be able to say which.

gaps.what: No bit-extraction, shift or mask converters in the expression language.
gaps.why: objectType = objectIdentifier >> 22; instance = objectIdentifier & 0x3FFFFF; dnetPresent = npduControl & 0x20; maxApduCode = byte1 & 0x0F; SEG = apduByte0 & 0x08. Every one is needed to interpret the captures. §6's converter table is closed and contains no shl/shr/and/or/bit. So even after a decode reads `objectIdentifier` as a u32be, nothing downstream can split it, and no `when` can test a control bit.

gaps.what: `tlv` cannot express a BACnet tag: the length lives INSIDE the tag octet, with three escapes, and the tag number has its own escape.
gaps.why: v0's `tlv` is `{"t":"u8","l":"u8","v":…}` — T and L as separate whole scalars of fixed width. A BACnet tag octet packs tagNumber(4) + class(1) + LVT(3): 0x0c, 0x19, 0x3e, 0x3f, 0x75, 0x91, 0xc4 in the captures. LVT 0-4 is the literal length; LVT 5 escapes to a following octet (0x75 0x0c at C2 offset 17), and if THAT octet is 254 a u16be follows, 255 a u32be; LVT 6/7 are opening/closing markers carrying no length at all; and tagNumber 15 escapes to a whole extra octet. `tlv` and `tlvList` are unusable for the single most common construct in the protocol.
gaps.proposedFix:
Generalise `tlv` to a packed, escaping descriptor:
{ "tlv": {
    "descriptor": { "bits":[ {"n":4,"as":"tagNumber"}, {"n":1,"as":"tagClass"},
                             {"n":3,"as":"lvt"} ] },
    "tagEscape": { "when":"tagNumber == 15", "read":"u8", "into":"tagNumber" },
    "lenFrom":   "lvt",
    "lenEscape": { "when":"lvt == 5", "read":"u8",
                   "chain":[ {"when":"== 254","read":"u16be"},
                             {"when":"== 255","read":"u32be"} ] },
    "markers":   { "open":6, "close":7 },
    "v": "…" } }
This also covers ASN.1 BER/DER long-form tags and lengths, so it earns its keep beyond BACnet.

gaps.what: No length-delimited sub-parse scope and no assertion field.
gaps.why: BVLC length (0x0020 in C2) bounds the whole datagram; NPDU+APDU parsing must be confined to bvlcLength - 4 octets, and a datagram whose actual size disagrees must be rejected rather than parsed into garbage. Real BACnet routers do emit wrong BVLC lengths. v0 has no `assert`, no `remaining()`, and no way to budget a field list. Related: 'parse tags until the end of the APDU' is a common BACnet idiom that needs `remaining() > 0` and is therefore also inexpressible.
gaps.proposedFix:
{ "scope": { "bytes": "capture.bvlcLength - 4",
              "onOverrun": "error", "onUnderrun": "error",
              "fields": [ /* npdu + apdu */ ] } }
Inside a `scope`, expose `remaining()` to expressions so `{"repeatUntil":"remaining() == 0"}` becomes writable. Add a standalone `{ "assert": "<expr>", "message":"…" }` field for cross-checks that are not scope-shaped.

gaps.what: `ref` takes no parameters and cannot recurse, so every repeated shape must be written out longhand.
gaps.why: The context-tag shape appears at C1 offsets 10 and 15, C2 offsets 9, 14, 16, 31, C3 offsets 11, 16, 18 — the same three-component bit-field with a different tag number and LVT each time. `{"ref":"messages.inner"}` nests a WHOLE message, which reads document-global `inputs.*`, so one ref site can only ever produce one value. And BACnet constructed data is genuinely recursive (opening tags inside opening tags), which an unparameterised, non-recursive `ref` cannot express at all.

gaps.what: No negotiated-capability primitive: the responder grants less than the requester proposed, twice, in one exchange.
gaps.why: C1 byte 6 bit 1 (SA=1) proposes that segmentation is acceptable; C1 byte 7 (0x25) proposes max-APDU 1476 and max 4 segments. The device may reply unsegmented (C2), or Abort with reason 4 segmentation-not-supported, or reason 1 buffer-overflow if the payload would exceed what was offered. Then C3 byte 9 counter-proposes a window size of 1, and C4 byte 9 grants it down to actual-window-size. Nothing in v0 records what was granted, so a LATER message cannot consult it. §5 lists this as a known gap (MQTT SUBACK); BACnet confirms it and adds the second, reverse-direction round.

gaps.what: No modal/exclusive device state, and no way to say that the failure mode is SILENCE.
gaps.why: After DeviceCommunicationControl(disable), a BACnet controller discards every APDU except DeviceCommunicationControl and ReinitializeDevice, for a specified duration, AND SENDS NOTHING BACK. On the wire that is byte-identical to a dropped UDP datagram and to a powered-off device. v0's `onTimeout` maps a timeout to exactly one successor state, so one observable (silence) with three meanings cannot be modelled. §5 lists modal state as a known gap; the silent-failure half is not even mentioned and is the part that actually bites in HVAC commissioning.

gaps.what: `confirmedBy` allows only one message and one predicate, so a success ACK that did not achieve the intended state cannot be diagnosed.
gaps.why: The BACnet case that matters most in HVAC: WriteProperty(present-value, priority 16) on a commandable object returns a SimpleACK — unambiguous success — while an existing priority-8 command keeps the physical output exactly where it was. The ACK confirms message acceptance and only PRESUMES effect. Confirming the effect needs a readback of present-value; explaining a mismatch needs a SECOND, DIFFERENT read (priority-array, or relinquish-default). §5's presume/confirmedBy shape is right in spirit but structurally one-shot.

gaps.what: Derived, reserved and non-canonical fields are normalised away, so encode(decode(bytes)) is not byte-identical.
gaps.why: Four concrete losses in these captures. (1) BVLC length is DERIVED on encode via len(group:bvll); a real router that emits a wrong length round-trips to a corrected one. (2) Reserved bits are dropped: APDU byte 7 bit 7 in C1 (0x25), NPDU control bits 6 and 4 in C1 (0x04), APDU byte 6 bit 0 in C1 (0x02) — a non-conforming device that sets any of them loses them. (3) Non-minimal encodings are legal on the wire but not preserved: a 4-octet value MAY arrive as LVT=5 + length octet 0x04 instead of LVT=4, and a length of 200 MAY arrive via the 254/u16be escape; decode captures only 'length = 4' and re-encodes the minimal form. (4) C4's NPDU control 0x04 vs 0x00 is a free encoder choice with no canonical answer. So round-trip fails in the encode(decode(bytes)) direction; decode(encode(x)) == x holds for C1/C2/C4/C5 only because I hard-coded the shapes.

gaps.what: `repeat` with a dynamic count is not documented, and `each` over a decoded count is shown only once.
gaps.why: NPDU's DADR field is exactly DLEN octets, where DLEN was decoded one field earlier; SADR is SLEN octets. §3's only `repeat` example is the literal `"repeat": 16`. The decode example does show `"each":"capture.byteCount / 2"`, so dynamic counts evidently exist somewhere — but whether `repeat` accepts an expression, in which mode, and whether it may reference `capture.*` mid-parse, is never stated. My decode block leans on `"each":"capture.valueLength - 1"` and I cannot prove it is legal.
gaps.proposedFix: State in §3 that `repeat`, `each`, `pad.to` and `skip` all accept any Int-valued expression in BOTH modes, and that in decode mode such an expression may reference any `capture.*` bound EARLIER in the same field list. Add the bound: the expression must be evaluable before the field is read, and a `limits.maxRepeat` caps it so the work bound stays computable.
